chosen.premise: If Krabby loses one pincer, it somehow becomes unable to walk sideways.
chosen.hook: Break one of Krabby’s claws, and it loses its signature movement.
chosen.visualIdea: Animate one pincer snapping off, followed by Krabby trying—and failing—to move sideways.
chosen.note: A precise, bizarre rule directly supported by two Pokédex entries: losing a pincer disables Krabby’s sideways movement.

candidates.visualIdea: Animate one pincer snapping off, followed by Krabby trying—and failing—to move sideways.
candidates.note: A precise, bizarre rule directly supported by two Pokédex entries: losing a pincer disables Krabby’s sideways movement.

candidates.premise: When it cannot find food, Krabby survives by swallowing a mouthful of sand for nutrients.
candidates.hook: When Krabby gets hungry, it eats sand.
candidates.visualIdea: Empty beach food search, then Krabby dramatically scoops up and swallows a mouthful of sand.
candidates.note: Extremely strange and specific survival behavior, fully supported by the Crystal entry; the swallowing action may need careful visual treatment to avoid implying unsupported biology.

candidates.premise: When danger approaches, Krabby blows bubbles around itself to look bigger.
candidates.hook: Krabby’s defense strategy is to fake being larger than it is.
candidates.visualIdea: Show a small Krabby suddenly surrounded by bubbles, making its silhouette appear much larger.
candidates.note: Clear and strongly supported defensive behavior with an excellent visual transformation, though the general idea of puffing up to appear threatening is somewhat familiar.

candidates.premise: Krabby’s pincers can break or be torn out in battle, yet they grow back fully.
candidates.hook: Krabby can lose a claw in battle—and grow it back.
candidates.visualIdea: Battle damage removes a pincer; a fast time-lapse shows the missing claw returning.
candidates.note: Strong, concrete regeneration premise with multiple supporting entries, but claw regrowth is less uniquely surprising than Krabby becoming unable to walk sideways.

candidates.premise: Krabby squabble over beach territory precisely where food is scarce.
candidates.hook: Krabby fights its neighbors when the beach has almost no food.
candidates.visualIdea: Wide beach shot reveals burrows, then cuts to Krabby confronting another over a patch of sand.
candidates.note: The food-scarcity connection is supported and filmable, but territorial animal conflict is a less startling hook and the angle is broader.

candidates.premise: Krabby’s pincers are weapons, but they also keep it balanced while walking sideways.
candidates.hook: Krabby’s claws aren’t just weapons—they’re part of its legs.
candidates.visualIdea: Split-screen: Krabby attacking with its pincers, then using them to balance during a sideways walk.
candidates.note: The balance function is distinctive and visual, but calling the pincers part of its legs overstates the cited entry; they assist balance rather than literally being legs.

rounds.request: None; this angle is strong enough. Stronger alternatives would need an equally specific, counterintuitive rule with direct Pokédex support and a clear visual payoff.
